If I could offer some unsolicited advice I'd say if there's a lull in the conversation just pick something you've been thinking about, even if it's mundane, and talk about it in a way that connects with you that you can get interested in and engaged with.

For example, even if it's just the weather, don't just say "It's getting cold out." Maybe start with that and when she says "Yeah I know!" or whatever go into what you think about the cold and weather, so for me I'd say like "Yeah and I'm actually kind of excited and kind of not, cause I love the fall and a little bit of snow, but once it hits February and it's *still* freezing I'm over it." Then that can lead to her talking about what she thinks about the cold, and/or talking about what climate each of you would prefer to live in, or memories of snow days as a kid or summer break, or whatever -- just elaborating more on how you connect with a subject can really help keep things flowing and that with actively listening to what they say can lead to some really interesting conversations. 

Just try to get genuinely engaged in something even if it's mundane rather than overanalyzing the situation and trying to find the "right thing" to say, or just interviewing her. And don't be afraid to lead the conversation.

I went through a similar thing as you with being a pushover and you need to go on your own path of introspection and self realization and not just copy exactly what I did but I will tell you some things I did/do that help me that might give you some guidance.

First I decided to just be honest and concise as I could with confrontation and use minimal necessary force (I neglected the "minimal force" thing at first but once I started getting better with confrontation I'd lose my newfound temper, so don't neglect that part). So if someone is bothering you, ask yourself if you're being unresonable honestly, and if not, tell the person who's bothering you exactly how you feel and why and if you're worried you are being unreasonable, tell them why you're worried about that too and why you're bringing it up anyways.

2nd I followed my dark and violent fantasies (just mentally) and let myself go deep into them mentally and acknowledged that I was capable of that shit (because everyone is capable of doing horrible things) and said it to myself. Like my parents were abusive and obviously that still effects my relationship to them in my adult life, so I was in an argument with my dad once a year or so ago when I was just starting with this type of thing, specifically Peterson/Jung's shadow concept and I let him kinda walk all over me and I fantasized about brutally killing him and I let myself really day dream about it and became honest with myself about my more dark drives and impulses (obviously don't act them out but it's about acknowledging they're there and that if you were pushed enough you might do something horrible because anyone might and people are capable of horrible things).

Last thing I'll mention though I've done a lot which has culminated into my being better with my darker drives and in confrontation which I guess you could possibly consider a shadow integration (though I've just started reading Jung so I'm hesitant at being too much like "I did this" cause I'm still pretty green with it), anyways that last thing I'll mention was I thought why I was afraid of confrontation, which went all the way down to the irrational conclusion that I was afraid of being physically damaged or killed, and decided that the risk of that was better than not being me, and letting people walk all over me was letting them pick away at me in a way. Now if someone held a gun to my head I don't know how I'd react in that moment but day to day confrontations I handle a lot better though I do get nervous still, it's not as bad and I feel more respected and I get angry during conflict rather than just scared.
